questions.question: You can use `*ngIf` and `[hidden]` to achieve exactly the same effect on the DOM.
questions.explanation: *ngIf removes the element from the DOM; [hidden] keeps it in the DOM but hides it.

questions.question: To enable two‑way data binding with `[(ngModel)]`, you must import `FormsModule`.
A pipe in Angular can change the original value of the component property.
questions.explanation: Pipes only transform the data for display; they do not mutate the original.

questions.question: Lazy loading reduces the initial bundle size by loading modules only when needed.
questions.explanation: Lazy‑loaded modules are loaded on demand, not at startup.

questions.question: Every Angular component must be declared in exactly one NgModule.
questions.explanation: A component can only belong to a single module. Standalone components are an exception (they don't need a module).

questions.question: You can navigate programmatically by injecting the `Router` service and calling `navigate()`.
questions.explanation: The Router service provides navigate() and navigateByUrl().

questions.question: `forkJoin` is used to combine multiple Observables and emits only after all complete.
questions.explanation: forkJoin waits for all source Observables to complete, then emits the last values.
